keyVerseText: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מַעְצוֹר (maʻtsôwr) derives from the root עָצָר (ʻâtsâr), which carries the fundamental idea of restraining, closing up, or holding back. This root conveys a physical sense of enclosing or shutting something in, as well as a metaphorical sense of withholding or refraining. Thus, מַעְצוֹר embodies the concept of restraint or hindrance, not merely as an obstacle but as an active force that can detain or limit movement or action. This enriches the English gloss 'restraint' by emphasizing both the power to hold back and the intentionality behind withholding.
usageInScripture: The word מַעְצוֹר appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Samuel 14:6, where it is translated as 'restraint.' Here, it conveys the absence of any hindrance or obstacle that might prevent the LORD from delivering His people, whether by many or by few. The singular occurrence and consistent translation highlight the word's focused meaning as a barrier or limitation that can be overcome by divine power. This usage underscores the idea that no human or circumstantial restraint can frustrate God's saving work.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מַעְצוֹר as a form of restraint or hindrance deepens our appreciation of God's sovereignty and power in salvation. It reminds believers that any obstacle—whether physical, spiritual, or circumstantial—is ultimately subject to God's authority and can be removed by His will. This word calls Christians to trust that no limitation can prevent God from acting on their behalf, reinforcing faith in His omnipotence. Furthermore, it encourages believers to recognize that God’s deliverance is not dependent on human strength or numbers but on His unrestricted ability to save. The concept also invites reflection on how God’s restraint may sometimes serve to teach patience and reliance on Him rather than on human resources.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Samuel 14:6, Jonathan declares there is 'no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few,' emphasizing God's unlimited power to deliver regardless of the odds. The term מַעְצוֹר here highlights that no hindrance can impede God's saving action, whether through large armies or small groups. This assurance encourages believers to trust boldly in God's ability to overcome any barrier, knowing that divine rescue transcends human limitations and obstacles.
